full_text:
Rookie draft weekend is here for many dynasty managers, including those playing in the [FFPC](https://myffpc.com/account/Login.aspx). Here are my Superflex PPR TE-Premium rankings. Happy hunting — let’s crush our leagues and walk away with the best possible selections.

\> If you are new to the [FFPC](https://myffpc.com/account/Login.aspx), use code POINTS at checkout for a free $25 credit!

A few notes:

+   If you play in single QB leagues, __Fernando Mendoza__ becomes a consideration in the early second round. You can ignore __Carson Beck__ entirely until the fourth or fifth round. Even in that range, he is a low upside bet.

+   If you play non-TE-premium, __Kenyon Sadiq__ should still be drafted in the same range, and Stowers doesn’t take too much of a knock either. They are both very strong prospects.
+   Be open-minded to trading your 2nd round picks for 2027 2nds if you are stuck on the clock and want to pick. The 2027 2nds will gain a lot of value this season and are way more obtainable than 2027 1sts.
+   Try to move up into the 1-4 range and the 5-8 range from the 9-12 range, even if it means paying more than usual. The top 7 picks are strong ones, despite the universal hatred for the 2026 class.
+   Be open-minded to drafting TEs. There are a number of players who can develop into starters
+   Embrace roster construction structure with handcuff RBs. There will be very few 2026 starters, but a number of players listed can become the #2 backs in their offenses.

__Theo Gremminger’s__ 2026 Superflex TE-Premium Dynasty Rankings
----------------------------------------------------------------

##### __1\. Jeremiyah Love,__ RB, Arizona Cardinals

The biggest no-brainer chalk 1.01 rookie draft pick in several years. Love is already a top-4 dynasty running back without even playing a down. He has the potential to be a future 1.01 in redraft in the near future. A soon-to-be 31-year-old __James Conner__ and __Tyler Allgeier__ are only minor impediments to a rookie year smash season.

{{CTA|FFPC|omit=\[none\]}}

{{PAYWALL}}

##### __2\. Carnell Tate,__ WR, Tennessee Titans

Alpha profile supported by alpha draft capital. Titans’ OC __Brian Daboll__ has overseen offenses that supported immediate impact WR1 smash seasons from __Malik Nabers__ (as a rookie) and __Stefon Diggs__ (acquired in a trade). Tate can be the next one. The market is vastly underestimating his ceiling in 2026. He is my WR13 overall in dynasty.

##### __3\. Jordyn Tyson,__ WR, New Orleans Saints

If you need a QB, you can push __Fernando Mendoza__ up to the 1.02, but head-to-head, give me Tyson. His ceiling is extremely high, and he will benefit from the pace of __Kellen Moore__’s scheme. The NFL isn’t worried about Tyson’s injury history, and you shouldn’t be either. He is very close to Tate. I believe both will be long-term high-end fantasy assets.

##### __4\. Fernando Mendoza,__ QB, Las Vegas Raiders

Mendoza will benefit from playing under __Klint Kubiak__ and already has an established #1 target in __Brock Bowers__. He also has #1 pick insulation with a long leash to fail. This is an easy bet to make for QB-needy teams. Mendoza is a major value when he falls to the 4th pick overall, and a consideration anywhere behind Love if you need a QB.

##### __5\. Makai Lemon,__ WR, Philadelphia Eagles

A number of sharp analysts are concerned about Lemon’s fit in the Eagles’ offense, but I think they are overthinking it. He has a clear path to early-career usage, especially with a potential __A.J. Brown__ trade likely after June 1. Both __Nick Sirianni__ and __Howie Roseman__ have praised his toughness, his ability to win both in the slot and outside, and his playmaking skills with the ball in his hands. __K.C. Concepcion__ is very close, and __Jadarian Price__ is also in the mix, but the edge goes to Lemon.

##### __6\. KC Concepcion,__ WR, Cleveland Browns

Concepcion is an electric talent and one of the best separators in this class. We have already seen how __Zay Flowers__ — a player with similar traits — was used in a __Todd Monken__ offense. The __Denzel Boston__ pick does nothing to diminish my enthusiasm for Concepcion.

##### __7\. Jadarian Price,__ RB, Seattle Seahawks

The Price faders and detractors are having to do some reshuffling this week. For those of us who were pounding the table for Price throughout the pre-draft process, his selection in the first round was pure vindication. He is a home run hitter who plays a lot like __Kenneth Walker,__ and is now taking over the Walker role in the Seattle offense. He can have a big 2026 season. If you are a contender or an RB-needy team, you can reach for him at 5, but I prefer him at 6 or 7.

##### __8\. Kenyon Sadiq,__ TE, New York Jets

There is a tier break after 7, but Sadiq is not a bad consolation prize. He has rare athleticism, blazing speed, and terrific draft capital. There is target competition with an established WR1, __Garrett Wilson__, as well as fellow rookie __Omar Cooper Jr.__ Don’t expect a Bowers or LaPorta type of rookie season, but Sadiq is already a fringe TE1 in dynasty.

##### __9\. Ty Simpson,__ QB, LA Rams

Simpson is easier to draft in large roster formats than in shallow dynasty leagues like the FFPC. He is a dynasty asset who will not lose value throughout the season and is a player with trade value for rebuilding managers all year long and into 2027.

##### __10\. Eli Stowers,__ TE, Philadelphia Eagles

Stowers has some 2025 __Harold Fannin Jr.__ parallels with his landing spot and situation — albeit with better draft capital and in a much better offensive environment. He is a mismatch/move tight end playing for a franchise that has hit big on their last two second-round picks at the position (__Zach Ertz, Dallas Goedert__). There are only three tight ends in SEC history with 60+ receptions in a season: __Brock Bowers, Evan Engram,__ and Stowers. Bowers and Engrameach went on to have at least one 100+ catch season at the NFL level.

##### __11\. Omar Cooper Jr.,__ WR, NY Jets

Cooper has to compete not only with Wilson, but also Sadiq in the long-term. Despite some hurdles to overcome, there’s a lot to his game that is fantasy-friendly. His YAC ability and toughness are traits that offensive coordinators gravitate towards. He could be a saving grace for managers, picking late in the first round this year.

##### __12\. Denzel Boston,__ WR, Cleveland Browns

Boston was drafted inside the top-40 picks, but lands in a difficult situation with Fannin Jr. and Concepcion to compete with. This is a bet on talent and draft capital, and it also has some downside risk.

##### __13\. Jonah Coleman,__ RB, Denver Broncos

The Denver backfield is crowded, but Coleman could win the favor of the Broncos’ coaching staff and be the lead back at some point this season. He has some very appealing traits for fantasy, including the ability to sustain volume and catch the ball out of the backfield. Coleman has the size to hold up over the course of an NFL season.

##### __14\. Antonio Williams,__ WR, Washington Commanders

Bernard and Williams are neck and neck for me, but long term, I lean toward Williams because of the landing spot. Besides __Terry McLaurin__, there is minimal competition. Long term, Williams could be the answer as a slot with YAC ability and manufactured touch capability attached to __Jayden Daniels__. This landing spot is *great*.

##### __15\. Germie Bernard,__ WR, Pittsburgh Steelers

__Mike McCarthy__ has elevated the trajectories of several power slots in the past, and Bernard fits this role very well. 2026 could be tricky with __DK Metcalf__ and __Michael Pittman Jr.__ to compete with, but both players will be 29 in 2027.

##### __16\. De’Zhuan Stribling,__ WR, San Francisco 49ers

Stribling went earlier than expected, but it is time to separate your feelings from the pick itself and focus on the opportunity at hand. __Mike Evans__ is old, and __Ricky Pearsall__ cannot stay on the field. __George Kittle’s__ return date and quality of play after injury are unknown. There is a non-zero chance that Stribling’s role could be similar to peak __Brandon Aiyuk’s__ at some point early in his career.

##### __17\. Eli Raridon,__ TE, New England Patriots

Raridson is big, fast, and uber athletic. He has a clear pathway to becoming New England’s starting TE in 2027, with a good chance of cutting into __Hunter Henry’s__ target share this season. We want skill position players attached to __Drake Maye__.

##### __18\. Zachariah Branch,__ WR, Atlanta Falcons

I understand the red flags, but I want to add Branch shares to my dynasty rosters. He has a clear pathway to becoming a significant part of Atlanta’s weekly game plan. And about the low aDOT screen heavy usage? There is no better fit that check down artist __Tua Tagovailoa__. There are some parallels between Branch in 2026 and __Tank Dell__ in 2023.

##### __19\. Ted Hurst,__ WR, Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Hurst is a very good upside bet to make in this range of the draft. He has an outstanding size-speed combination (6-4, 4.42 40) and can fill an immediate role as a big outside threat on a Bucs offense that needs one. There will be a target competition in 2026, but if the team moves on from __Chris Godwin__ next offseason, Hurst could be a 2027 starter.

##### __20\. Nicholas Singleton,__ RB, Tennessee Titans

Singleton fell to Day 3, but landed well. He was mega productive in college before a disappointing 2026 season, but has athleticism, size, and pass-catching ability. Day 3 backs (__Tyrone Tracy__ in 2024, __Cam Skattebo__ in 2025) earned large roles in Daboll offenses the past two seasons. Singleton could make it three in a row.

##### __21\. Chris Bell,__ WR, Miami Dolphins

Bell is available in this range of rookie drafts because he is coming off a torn ACL. The Dolphins selected him in the 3rd round, but he has a runway to become their most productive WR in fantasy as soon as he steps on the field.

##### __22\. Oscar Delp,__ TE, New Orleans Saints

Delp is an exciting athletic TE prospect with blazing speed. Much like Raridon, his 2026 pathway could be tricky with __Juwan Johnson__ ahead of him on the roster, but he will likely take over in 2027 and have a few eye-opening big plays this season.

##### __23\. Carson Beck,__ QB, Arizona Cardinals

Beck is a good bet to start some games this year for Arizona. I have concerns over his long-term outlook, especially with a loaded 2027 QB class on the way, but there is a small chance he proves a lot of people wrong and becomes this year’s __Tyler Shough__. From a game theory perspective, taking a QB in this range of Superflex drafts makes sense.

##### __24\. Max Klare,__ TE, LA Rams

Klare can overcome a crowded Rams’ TE room and become the team’s clear starter at the position heading into 2027. He will be on the field a lot this season due to LA’s high use of heavy personnel.

##### __25\. Emmett Johnson,__ RB, Kansas City Chiefs

High-end handcuff role behind __Ken Walker__ with pass-catching upside in a good offense. Can he carve out a weekly role in the passing game?

##### __26\. Chris Brazzell__ WR, Carolina Panthers

Will compete with __Jalen Coker__ for targets opposite __Tetairoa McMilan__. Has size/speed.

##### __27\. Justin Joly,__ TE, Denver Broncos

A move TE with juice. Joly can become Denver’s starting TE early in his career.

##### __28\. Kaytron Allen,__ RB, Washington Commanders

Allen fell to the sixth round, but he can become this season’s version of __Kyle Monangai__.

##### __29\. Kaelon Black,__ RB, San Francisco 49ers

Head-scratching draft capital, but in the driver’s seat for the handcuff role behind CMC.

##### __30\. Elijah Sarratt,__ WR, Baltimore Ravens

Push him up above the two running backs listed at 29/30 if you are a rebuilding team or need a wideout. He can become the Ravens’ WR2.

##### __31\. Skyler Bell,__ WR, Buffalo Bills

Uber-productive in college with strong athletic measurables. Could earn a solid role in this offense.

##### __32\. Mike Washington,__ RB, Las Vegas Raiders

Horrible landing spot with no shot at earning a starting job barring injury. Put him in the high-end handcuff contingent upside category. Prioritize if you have __Ashton Jeanty__ on your roster.

##### __33\. Demond Claiborne,__ RB, Minnesota Vikings

Speedy back in a good offense. Can carve out a __Keaton Mitchell__\-esque role.

##### __34\. Adam Randall,__ RB, Baltimore Ravens

A good bet to win the handcuff role in Baltimore.

##### __35\. Caleb Douglas,__ WR, Miami Dolphins

Can earn a starting role this season. Drafted ahead of Bell.

##### __36\. Taylen Green,__ QB, Cleveland Browns

Elite athletic traits. Incredible tools. But the downside is complete zero return.

##### __37\. Cyrus Allen,__ WR, Kansas City Chiefs

Athletic deep threat.

##### __38\. Malachi Fields,__ WR, NY Giants

Can earn the starting role opposite __Malik Nabers__. Massive size for a wideout.

##### __39\. Ja’Kobi Lane,__ WR, Baltimore Ravens

Drafted ahead of Sarratt.

##### __40\. Drew Allar,__ QB, Pittsburgh Steelers

Discount __Carson Beck__.

### OTHER OPTIONS

##### __Cole Payton,__ QB, Philadelphia Eagles

##### __Tanner Koziol,__ TE, Jacksonville Jaguars

##### __Bryce Lance,__ WR, New Orleans Saints

##### __Brenen Thompson,__ WR, LA Chargers

##### __Matthew Hibner,__ TE, Baltimore Ravens

\> If you are new to the [FFPC](https://myffpc.com/account/Login.aspx), use code POINTS at checkout for a free $25 credit!
